import numpy as np

# Paper money in circulation (in millions) from FY 1941 to FY 1948 (from 1948 bulletin)
# and FY 1949 to FY 1950 (from 1950 bulletin)
data = [8932, 11600, 16492, 21438, 25541, 26945, 26942, 26482, 26034, 25661]

print("Data (paper money in circulation, millions):")
for i, (year, val) in enumerate(zip(range(1941, 1951), data)):
    print(f"FY {year}: {val}")

# Calculate unbiased sample Fisher excess Kurtosis
# Formula: g2 = [n(n+1) / ((n-1)(n-2)(n-3))] * (sum((xi - mean)^4) / s^4) - 3(n-1)^2 / ((n-2)(n-3))

n = len(data)
mean = np.mean(data)
std = np.std(data, ddof=1)  # sample standard deviation
print(f"\nn = {n}")
print(f"Mean = {mean}")
print(f"Std (sample) = {std}")

# Calculate the fourth moment
fourth_moment = np.mean((np.array(data) - mean)**4)
print(f"Fourth moment = {fourth_moment}")

# Calculate the kurtosis
# Using the formula for unbiased sample Fisher excess kurtosis
m4 = np.sum((np.array(data) - mean)**4) / n  # 4th moment about the mean
s4 = std**4

#Fisher excess kurtosis formula (unbiased)
# g2 = ((n+1)*n*kurtosis - 3*(n-1)^2) / ((n-2)*(n-3))
# where kurtosis = m4 / s^4

kurtosis = m4 / s4  # This is the population kurtosis (not excess)
print(f"Pearson kurtosis = {kurtosis}")

# Unbiased Fisher excess kurtosis
# Using the formula: γ2 = [n(n+1) / ((n-1)(n-2)(n-3))] * Σ(xi-x̄)^4 / s^4 - 3(n-1)² / ((n-2)(n-3))

numerator1 = n * (n + 1)
denominator1 = (n - 1) * (n - 2) * (n - 3)
term1 = numerator1 / denominator1 * (np.sum((np.array(data) - mean)**4) / std**4)

numerator2 = 3 * (n - 1)**2
denominator2 = (n - 2) * (n - 3)
term2 = numerator2 / denominator2

g2 = term1 - term2
print(f"\nUnbiased sample Fisher excess kurtosis = {g2}")
print(f"Rounded to 3 decimal places = {round(g2, 3)}")

# Alternative calculation using scipy
from scipy import stats
g2_scipy = stats.kurtosis(data, fisher=True, bias=False)
print(f"\nUsing scipy.stats.kurtosis (fisher=True, bias=False): {g2_scipy}")
